memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then it continued eastward to Gath Hepher and Eth Kazin; it came out at Rimmon and turned toward Neah. There the boundary went around on the north to Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Iphtah El. Included were Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem. There were twelve towns and their villages. These towns and their villages were the inheritance of Zebulun, according to its clans - Josh 19:13-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The description of Zebulun's land is completed with a list of its towns — twelve in all. Among them is Gath Hepher, which is worth pausing over. Gath Hepher was the hometown of the prophet Jonah (2 Kings 14:25). This ordinary town in Zebulun's portion would one day produce the reluctant prophet whom God sent to the great pagan city of Nineveh.

It is striking that God raised up a prophet from this modest northern town, and even more striking what that prophet's story would come to mean. Jonah, three days in the belly of the great fish and then delivered, became a sign that Jesus Himself pointed to — a picture of His own death and resurrection after three days (Matt 12:40). A town in Zebulun's inheritance is quietly tied, across the centuries, to the greatest event in history.

We can never fully know what God intends to bring out of the ordinary places and people in His story. Gath Hepher was just one of twelve towns in one tribe's portion, yet God had purposes for it that reached all the way to the resurrection of Christ. This gives dignity to the ordinary. The unremarkable town, the overlooked place, the modest beginning — none is beneath God's use. He delights to bring significant things out of small and hidden places for His glory.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does it surprise you that God raised a prophet from an ordinary town like Gath Hepher?
- How does the "sign of Jonah" pointing to Christ deepen your view of God's plan?
- Do you believe God can bring significant things from ordinary places, including your life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You bring great purposes out of ordinary places. Help me to trust that no place or person is beneath Your use, and to serve You faithfully wherever I am. Amen.
